Streets, schools and getting around Buying a Chicken Farm in BC

items.t: Scope: broiler chicken farms anywhere in British Columbia — there is no neighbourhood, no MLS sub-area and no street boundary for this guide; the location facts for any real purchase are the farm's municipality and its Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status, checked parcel by parcel.

Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere — a chicken farm purchase combines ALR land, broiler barns and other farm buildings, a principal residence and possibly one additional residence, plus, separately and only if the contract states it, production quota; no strata lot appears anywhere in that package. states the zero in full.

Where BC chicken production is concentrated, as an official-source statement: Not confirmed — the guide's statement that the vast majority of BC poultry production sits in the Fraser Valley, with Abbotsford and Chilliwack holding the bulk, is site copy only; no Province agricultural-plan or land-use-inventory source was opened.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Buying a Chicken Farm in BC

items.t: : ALR residences cannot be stratified. Depositing a strata plan causes subdivision in the ALR and needs ALC permission — ALC Information Bulletin 09, s.6; see also Strata Property Act s.239 and Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1). Subdivision of ALR land generally requires ALC approval.

ALR residence frame: on ALR land, one principal residence is permitted without an ALC application at a maximum total floor area of 500 m² (no more than 1,000 m² of fill), a secondary suite is permitted only when located within the principal residence, and at most one additional residence is permitted of up to 90 m² on properties 40 ha or less or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha; local government bylaws may further regulate or restrict residences, and may not be more permissive than the ALC's requirements. The guide's statement that ALR rules generally allow barns, a principal residence and, with restrictions, additional dwellings is consistent with this frame at that general level. Those are houses on one title — neither is a condo unit.

Quota, supply management and the BCCMB transfer process — not confirmed in every particular: that BC chicken production is supply managed in the terms the page states; the BCCMB's licensing, minimum-pricing and production-control mandate; how quota is measured; that quota never transfers automatically and that a share sale is still a quota transaction; the joint seller/buyer application and Board review of buyer, site and transaction; the Board cancelling the seller's quota and allotting quota to the buyer; the Board-approved-building condition; any quota price or valuation basis; and the guide's three-routes-in framing, including buying quota separately onto an approved site.

Small-flock thresholds — not confirmed: the guide states up to 200 birds a year for personal use without a permit; a Small Lot Permit between 200 and 2,000 birds (annual application, $20 fee, one permit per site, Premises ID registration, yearly placement and processing reports, inspected-facility processing); and up to 99 hens on the egg side with no quota or registration — no board or Province small-lot source was opened, so none of those figures is adopted.

Form B (contrast only — no strata lot exists in this topic): Strata Property Act s. 59 — on a resale purchase the strata must provide a Form B Information Certificate stating strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and a summary of the strata's insurance, with rules, budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

Depreciation reports and CRF (strata-wide, contrast only): since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, no deferral by vote; and since November 1, 2023, stratas must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF.

Rentals and age (strata-wide, contrast only): rental-restriction bylaws are VOID since November 24, 2022 for strata property anywhere in BC, and the only valid age bylaw is a 55+ bylaw under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 and Regulation 7.01, with exemptions for legacy residents, live-in caregivers and (from May 1, 2023) younger spouses/partners and defined children. Neither rule touches a freehold chicken farm — there is no strata corporation.

GST and rebates (residence side only): 5% GST applies to new construction, not resales. First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 — secondary sources saying March 12 are superseded): 100% of GST to $1M, maximum $50,000, phasing to $1.5M, agreements March 20, 2025–2031; GST New Housing Rebate 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350,000–$450,000 phase-out. How GST is apportioned between land, buildings, residence and quota on a specific chicken-farm purchase: Not confirmed — no Province farm-transfer tax source was opened.

items.t: There is no neighbourhood, no MLS sub-area and no street boundary for this guide; the location facts for any real purchase are the farm's municipality and its Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status, checked parcel by parcel.

The other pole of the standing feed tension, stated explicitly: the poultry-sector listing pages this guide links onward to (broiler, egg, turkey, chicken and poultry-farms-for-sale-bc) carry GENERIC feeds — their cards are never confirmed operations in the named sector — while THIS page carries no feed at all. A reader therefore cannot treat a sector-page card as a confirmed poultry operation, and cannot treat this guide as a listings source; both positions hold at once.
How people search for it: "buying a chicken farm BC," "how to buy a chicken farm," "chicken quota BC transfer," "BCCMB quota transfer," "broiler farm buying guide."

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Buying a Chicken Farm in BC

items.t: ALR block (province-wide frame, ALC): on ALR land, one principal residence is permitted without an ALC application at a maximum total floor area of 500 m² (no more than 1,000 m² of fill), a secondary suite is permitted only when located within the principal residence, and at most one additional residence is permitted of up to 90 m² on properties 40 ha or less or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha; local government bylaws may further regulate or restrict residences, and may not be more permissive than the ALC's requirements. Subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval, and strata plans in the ALR cause subdivision per ALC Information Bulletin 09 s.6; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)).

Municipal frames — stated per labelled example, never blended: this guide is province-wide, so no single municipality's zoning, servicing or tax frame is applied to it. Abbotsford's Development Bylaw number and Chilliwack's servicing number, stay not confirmed).

PTT — worked example (inputs + tier math, general tiers only): on a $2,000,000 farm purchase at general tiers — 1% on the first $200,000 ($2,000) + 2% on $200,000–$2,000,000 ($36,000) = $38,000. Tiers: 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion over $3,000,000.

GST — CRA GI-003 level only: developer/business sales and newly subdivided lots generally TAXABLE; an individual's sale of personal-use land generally exempt; finer points not confirmed, and GST apportionment between land, buildings, residence and quota on a farm purchase is not verified here on the same basis as PTT above.

Strata block (for completeness — no strata stock in this topic): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF since November 1, 2023; rental bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). An ALR farm residence carries none of this unless a strata plan is filed — which itself needs ALC approval (above).
